blocks.text: Such sources can be classified as either mobile (cars, trucks, air planes, marine engines) or point sources (factories, electric power plants etc.). The combustion of fossil fuels (coal, fuel oils, and natural gas) in vehicle engines, factories and power plants produce carbon dioxide (CO₂) carbon-monoxide (CO), and hydrocarbons (CH₄). The burning of wood as a domestic fuel and coal in brick kilns are also the sources of air pollutants.

blocks.explanation: Oxides of carbon (CO, CO₂), oxides of nitrogen (NOₓ), oxides of sulphur (SOₓ), hydrocarbons, low-altitude ozone (O₃), CFCs, PAHs, POPs, VOCs, particulate matter (PM) and heavy metals (Pb, Hg, Cd).

blocks.prompt: b) Give the equations for the formation and depletion of ozone in the stratosphere.
blocks.explanation:
In the upper stratosphere ozone absorbs UV light and breaks down: O₃(g) →(hν) O₂(g) + O(g).
In the middle stratosphere ozone forms: O₂(g) + O(g) → O₃(g), an exothermic reaction.

blocks.prompt: c) Write down the names and approximate height of different layers of atmosphere.
blocks.explanation: Troposphere 0–12 km, stratosphere 12–50 km, mesosphere 50–85 km and thermosphere 85–600 km.
